$comment: T7 (Agent 5): the REVIEWED BEHAVIOUR-CHANGE CATALOGUE for the permanent owner login (owner addendum 2026-11-04).
Every protection the restricted runtime logins (crewflow_app / crewflow_worker) gave that the owner login crewflow_owner cannot keep is one entry here,
with a severity, the test that proves the new behaviour, and its acceptance status: OWNER-ACCEPTED (the owner's final prompt section 2) or
NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not listed there). The final removal PR (#9) is gated on: every entry has a passing test, no entry is NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL,
and every existing test that asserted restricted-login behaviour is listed under migratedTests (migrated to this catalogue, or kept as a schema-role test).
A test is never flipped to 'passes' because the owner can now do the thing: the new behaviour is asserted AND recorded as a finding.

differences.change: The runtime login reads every tenant's rows of the 16 NOT FORCE pre-auth tables without injection (a missing tenant filter suffices).
differences.mitigation: M-T1 (FORCE + owner-only definer policy) protects normal code paths only

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: loss of column-level secret grants)
differences.change: Column grants no longer hide core."user".password_hash, totp_secret_encrypted, temporary_password_hash, totp_last_used_step from the runtime login.

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: SQL injection with owner privileges; policy modification; object deletion)
differences.change: Injected SQL has full DDL: NO FORCE / DISABLE RLS, ALTER POLICY USING (true), DROP TABLE, DROP SCHEMA core CASCADE.
differences.mitigation: semantic posture hash at boot and on a timer (M0 §6.4 #4)

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: account takeover and MFA bypass)
differences.change: SET ROLE rab_secure_owner or DISABLE TRIGGER defeats the MFA column guard: cross-tenant MFA writes.
differences.keptControl: the guard still refuses a direct write by the owner login on a normal path (C4, CONTROL-HOLDS)

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: persistence through roles or definers; credential-exposure impact)
differences.change: Backdoor LOGIN roles, re-granting the schema owner, replacing SECURITY DEFINER bodies, resetting crewflow_app's password survive rotation of the owner password.
differences.mitigation: incident runbook: rotation is not remediation; drop unknown roles

differences.change: audit_log append-only no longer holds against the runtime: it can GRANT itself UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE (owner of the table via membership).
differences.keptControl: UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE are absent from the table owner's own ACL, so the owner login is refused on every normal path (C3, CONTROL-HOLDS)
differences.mitigation: external append-only audit sink is MANDATORY (M0 §3.4)

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: deployment identity rebindable by the runtime)
differences.change: deployment_identity_bind admits the runtime login (EXECUTE via rab_secure_owner, session login is a member and is not crewflow/crewflow_app).
differences.mitigation: D6: deployment id mandatory after the first bind; bind only on an empty database

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: loss of DBA-01 API/Worker separation)
differences.change: The API process can execute every crewflow_worker-only definer (dispatch claims, release, invite cleanup) and the due-work functions, and terminate the Worker's sessions.

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: worker_due_work and pointer direct access)
differences.change: Direct SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on core.worker_due_work across tenants without a definer; dispatch pointers and the deployment marker after SET ROLE.

differences.acceptance: OWNER-ACCEPTED (§2: SQL injection with owner privileges)
differences.change: A session-level set_config('role', ..., false) survives COMMIT: pool poisoning of later requests.
differences.mitigation: RESET ROLE/DISCARD ALL on checkout + current_user = session_user assertion (mandatory, M0 §6.4 #3)

differences.change: The workspace registry versioning guard is a deny-list (current_user <> 'crewflow_app'), so the runtime may write drift/version columns.

differences.acceptance: NEEDS OWNER APPROVAL (not in §2: no logical backup by the app login, PITR only)
differences.change: A pg_dump with the only credential the deployment holds dumps every FORCE tenant table empty.
16 NOT FORCE pre-auth tables, not 15: organisation_invitation is missing from CLAUDE.md.

hardFloors.$comment: Real security properties that still hold for the owner login (HARD-FLOOR / CONTROL-HOLDS findings, PASS).
tests: twenty-behaviour-catalogue C1b, C3/acl, C4/mfa-guard, C4b, C8/superuser

migratedTests.$comment: Existing suites that assert restricted-runtime-login behaviour. Each must end as: 'catalogue:<id>' (migrated, the difference is above), 'schema-role' (kept: it tests a schema role that still exists, e.g. a definer running as rab_secure_owner), or 'unchanged' (passes as the owner login without asserting a weaker property). Filled from the TW-D differential (run the suite with TEST_DATABASE_URL = crewflow_owner).
migratedTests.status: first pass pending: see the T7 report for the TW-D results
